subject.title: [Bug]: Codex OAuth refresh succeeds but cron/heartbeat fail with 10s auth refresh timeout

question: Should OpenClaw mitigate the Codex app-server 10-second external-auth refresh callback in its own auth bridge, or wait for upstream Codex configurability while keeping this issue open as the canonical tracker?
rationale: Current main has partial fixes, but the remaining behavior crosses OpenClaw's provider/auth policy and upstream Codex's callback contract, so automation should not choose the product boundary unilaterally.

options.title: Mitigate in OpenClaw bridge
options.body: Return cached usable tokens or otherwise avoid forced refresh work inside the upstream 10-second callback, with status/error coverage for degraded auth.

options.title: Wait for upstream configurability
options.body: Keep this issue open and track the upstream Codex timeout request, accepting that OpenClaw users may still hit the 10-second callback failure until Codex changes.

options.title: Split remaining work
options.body: Close only the revoked-token masking subproblem under the merged fixes and leave this issue or a narrower follow-up for valid-but-slow refresh callbacks.

recommendation.title: Mitigate in OpenClaw bridge
recommendation.body: Return cached usable tokens or otherwise avoid forced refresh work inside the upstream 10-second callback, with status/error coverage for degraded auth.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent direct Codex contract verification and merge activity on the app-server refresh error path make this the strongest available owner signal for the boundary decision.
